title: Week 19 Reading Quiz
description_html: Read both lessons before you start. Choose the best answer for each question. You may take this quiz twice, and your higher score counts.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.text_html: Mexican leaders refused to receive John Slidell, and President Herrera was overthrown partly because people thought he would talk. Which conclusion about Mexican politics in 1845 is best supported?

answers.text: A Mexican leader who seemed ready to accept the Río Grande border could be attacked at home.
Mexican leaders were eager for war and saw no value in any money offered for land.
Mexico's leaders were sure the United States would never send an army to the border.
Most Mexican voters wanted their government to sell California to the United States quickly.

questions.name: Question 2
questions.text_html: General Taylor marched to the Río Grande in 1846 and built a fort across from Matamoros. How would Mexican officers most likely have described this move?

answers.text: A friendly visit meant to protect Texas settlers from raids.
A retreat from the disputed strip back toward Corpus Christi.
An American army entering land that Mexico claimed as its own.
A trade mission to the Mexican city of Matamoros.

questions.name: Question 3
questions.text_html: Congressman Abraham Lincoln later asked President Polk to name the exact spot where American blood had been shed. What was Lincoln really questioning?

answers.text: Whether the American soldiers who died had been killed by Mexican troops or by accident.
Whether the fight had taken place on land that truly belonged to the United States.
Whether Congress had the power to declare war without the President.
Whether Mexico had a standing army able to threaten Texas.

questions.name: Question 4
questions.text_html: Jack Hays and Samuel Walker led Texas Rangers in the army. Which fact best explains why army officers valued them as scouts?

answers.text: They rode fast, shot well from horseback, and Walker knew Mexico from being held prisoner there.
They had been trained for years in the army's engineering school and knew how to build bridges and forts.
They were the only soldiers in the army who could speak Spanish fluently.
They had never fought in a battle before the war with Mexico began.

questions.name: Question 5
questions.text_html: After Taylor's victories at Monterrey and Buena Vista, Polk still sent a second army under Winfield Scott to Veracruz. What best explains the decision?

answers.text: Taylor had been defeated at Buena Vista, and Polk needed a second army to rescue him from Santa Anna.
Mexico's leaders still refused to give up land, so Polk chose to strike at the capital.
Congress had ordered Polk to bring the war to an end by the spring.
Scott wanted to protect the Texas frontier from Comanche raids.

questions.name: Question 6
questions.text_html: Under the Compromise of 1850, Texas gave up claims to land around Santa Fe and received $10 million. What does this show about Texas after 1845?

answers.text: Texas could keep settling its borders and its debts on its own without ever turning to the national government.
Texas had been forced out of the United States over its western claims.
Texas no longer had any debts and no longer claimed the Río Grande.
Questions about its boundaries and debts were now settled through the national government.
